messages.author: 0c39e60ddb38622b
messages.subject: Re: Several values for each year
parts:
Uh, no. The OP has 5 values in 1986 and 4 in 2005. For a boxplot, one
should have at least 20 observations per group, preferably 30 or more.
In this case, I'd suggest a strip chart, which is simply a
geom_point() layer, perhaps one of the following:

library(ggplot2)

DF <- data.frame(X1, X2)

# Treats X2 as numeric
ggplot(DF, aes(x = X2, y = X1)) + geom_point()

# Treats X2 as factor
ggplot(DF, aes(x = factor(X2), y = X1)) + geom_point() +
labs(x = "X2")

Another problem with boxplots or error bars in this context is that
they don't reflect the large difference in sample size in 2004
relative to 1986 or 2005 unless you add sample size annotations
somewhere in the graphics region.

Alternatives if one only wants to visualize point ranges include
geom_pointrange() and geom_linerange(). See the on-line help for
additional details: docs.ggplot2.org/current

Dennis
